note: Bottomland hardwood and wetland area beside Mingo National Wildlife Refuge. The area map marks two camps: this one, a long gravel strip beside the area office and Cypress Pond on the east side, and a gravel loop on the south levee road of Pool 1, a 1,800-acre reservoir. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: area page 'Designated Camping Sites'; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted only in designated areas on the area map', 14 days in 30. Map (11/3/2022) has two campfire symbols: by the office/Cypress Pond (GIS 37, the pin) and on Pool 1's south levee (GIS 38, 3.8 km SW). Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. Pin fine. Split proposed for the Pool 1 camp. Not waterfront kept for the pin. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted only in designated areas on the area map and stays are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period... Groups of 10 or more campers must obtain a special use permit.' Map shows a campfire symbol (unlabelled in the legend) beside a P, privy and accessible symbol at the office by Cypress Pond, and another on the Pool 1 south levee beside fish cleaning, jetty, P and accessible symbols. GIS camping layer: 37 and 38, both 'Primitive Camping Area'. Imagery: camp 37 is a ~90 x 25 m gravel strip under scattered trees between the office lot and the highway; camp 38 is a ~70 m gravel loop in woods just south of the levee road. A 23-ft rig fits both; reached on paved highway and MDC improved roads. No ford/4WD/rig wording.
PIN: stored 37.04615,-90.07356 = GIS 37 on the gravel camp strip (office lot 1784 30 m W). Fine.

SPLIT proposed (1): 'Duck Creek Conservation Area (Pool 1 camp)' at 37.0225,-90.1041 (GIS 38 / lot 537), state/MDC, same groups and season, phone 573-222-3337. It is 3.8 km SW of the pin, reached by the Pool 1 south levee road from Highway 51 rather than from the office road, and is a separate gravel loop. No existing entry within 3 km (campgrounds.json checked). Waterfront for it: Pool 1 is ~60-80 m north of the camp point across the levee road (a road between), so not lakefront; a view of the pool from the loop's north edge is plausible but not shown, so not waterfront unless AWH reads it as lakeview. Its fall status: the map's Pool 1 South waterfowl refuge closes Oct 15 to end of duck season; whether the levee camp falls inside the closed zone is not legible on the map - the stored season note covers it.

WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept for the pin): Cypress Pond is a small pond ~60 m NE across the entrance area; the camp strip itself sits beside the highway with no open water edge. Pool 1 is ~2 km W.
Season (manual, year-round with the waterfowl-closure note) left as stored.
Note rewritten: acreage, generic MDC text, the 14-day limit (now booking.max_stay_nights) and directions dropped; where the two camps are put in.
